metadata.description: The measurement of a documentation package's declared learning path (PROP-057 `##NAV-CHAPTERS`, `##NAV-CHAPTERS-CHECKED`). `vibe doc check --chapters --json` prints exactly one of these. It answers one question — how often the path sends a reader ahead of itself — because every link from a page to a page the path reaches LATER is a place where the text needs something it has not taught yet. It is a MEASURER and never a gate: the norm rules the forward links a report rather than a verdict, because an orientation page points ahead ON PURPOSE, and a gate here would teach an author that the way to a green run is to stop writing the page that tells a reader where they are. Nothing in it is zero because nobody looked — a package that declared no path carries `measured = false`, and a page the pivot could not read is named in `unreadable` rather than counted clean. Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_chapters/`.
How many chapters the path declares. Zero means the package declared no path, which is the one state `measured` is false for.
How many pages stand on the path. A page two chapters both name stands on it once, because the path takes a reader past it once.

Every link that points ahead, page by page in the order the path walks them and, within a page, in the order the prose writes them. Written even when empty: «no link points ahead» is the answer a clean path gives, and a missing key would read as a measurement nobody took.

How many there are — the number a machine reads without counting the list, and the one figure this report exists to produce (`##NAV-CHAPTERS-CHECKED`). A floor rather than an answer while `unreadable` is not empty.
Pages the pivot refused, by their path under the spec root. Their links are unknown, and an unknown is not an absence, so the count above is a floor while this list has anything in it.

`false` for a package that declared no path, and the reason every other row is not read as a clean result: «no link points ahead» and «nobody declared an order» print the same digit and mean opposite things. A package without a path is not walked at all, so the numbers beside this are zero because nothing was asked.

One link that sends a reader ahead of where the path has taken them. Two kinds of link are not here and both fall out of one rule rather than a special case: a link INTO a chapter declared `appendix = true` is excepted, because looking a term up in the glossary is not being sent ahead of the lesson, and a fragment alone names a place on the page that says it, which is no link to another page in any reading (`##NAV-CHAPTERS-CHECKED`).
The document that carries the link, as a `[navigation]` row spells a page: under the spec root, without the extension.
The document it points at — further along the path than `page`.
